title: Career roadmap · Social Entrepreneur
summary: Build the ability to identify social problems, design sustainable solutions, understand communities, mobilise resources, and build an organisation that creates measurable social impact.

facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap assumes a 4-year BA Honours pathway from 2026–2030. If your university follows a 3-year BA, bring the final-year venture-building and fieldwork milestones into Year 3. The most useful approach is to combine humanities/social-science knowledge with entrepreneurship, communication, basic finance, programme design and real community exposure.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Identify a genuine social problem, conduct field research, build a small pilot solution and learn entrepreneurship fundamentals.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Develop a sustainable social enterprise, join an impact organisation or pursue postgraduate study in development, public policy, social entrepreneurship or management.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Scale the organisation, build partnerships, develop impact measurement and create sustainable revenue/funding systems.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Become an impact leader, ecosystem builder, investor/advisor, policy contributor or founder of a larger social-impact organisation.

blocks.text: 4-year honours variant

Use the additional academic depth for a substantial field-research dissertation or social-enterprise project. Ideally, the project should identify a measurable problem, involve community stakeholders, test a solution and evaluate its results.

blocks.text: Develop the ability to scale impact without losing sight of the communities being served. Strong social entrepreneurs combine field knowledge with financial sustainability, evidence-based decision-making, partnerships, technology and impact measurement.

Career progression

items: Programme Associate / Social Impact Associate (0–3 years)
Programme Manager / Social Innovation Manager (3–7 years)
Social Enterprise Founder / Impact Lead (5–10 years)
Senior Impact Leader / Organisation Head (10–15 years)
Social Venture Founder / Ecosystem Builder / Impact Consultant (15+ years)

blocks.text: Unlike a conventional corporate career, social entrepreneurship can begin much earlier if the student successfully identifies a problem and builds a viable solution.
PhD routes
Possible research directions include:
A PhD is most useful for research, university teaching, policy work and advanced impact-sector research rather than being necessary for founding a social enterprise.

The strongest long-term position is to become an impact builder, not just an NGO administrator. Build systems that can survive beyond individual grants or projects. Strong social entrepreneurs understand community needs, revenue models, partnerships, impact measurement, technology, policy and organisational leadership. AI can improve research, communication and operational efficiency, but genuine community participation and measurable outcomes remain central.
